declared_purpose: Provide Lark calendar-event and task CRUD, event listing, attendee/member management, and employee-name-to-user_id resolution (SKILL.md:2-16, 74-104, 122-179). Explicit settings and rules include credential configuration, default calendar/timezone, datetime and identifier formats, and automatic Boyang attendance. Bulk directory retrieval, cached contact fields, notifications, reminders and diagnostic output are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Request local configuration loading and read credentials
data_operations.source: lib/lark-api.mjs module initialization; dotenv and process.env
data_operations.data_scope: The .secrets.env path four levels above the library directory; FEISHU_APP_ID and FEISHU_APP_SECRET.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local dotenv dependency and process memory.
data_operations.condition: On module import, before command validation or help handling. The dependency's actual file-reading behavior is not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate, cache a bearer token, and send authenticated requests
data_operations.data_scope: Application credentials sent for authentication; bearer token, endpoint identifiers, query parameters and operation bodies sent on subsequent calls.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal and the applicable Lark API endpoint; token and expiry retained in process memory.
data_operations.condition: An API invocation authenticates when the cached token is unavailable or near expiry. Error code 99991663 clears the token and recursively replays the request without an enforced retry limit.

data_operations.operation: Persist an employee directory in packaged source
data_operations.source: SKILL.md employee table and lib/employees.mjs FALLBACK_EMPLOYEES
data_operations.data_scope: Names, aliases and user_ids for 21 employees; documentation additionally associates employees with organizational roles.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Public package documentation/source and its readers; fallback records can also enter process memory.
data_operations.condition: Present on package distribution. Fallback records are used when dynamic retrieval fails. Roles are supplied assertions, not computed attributes.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve directory pages and cache contact records
data_operations.data_scope: Requests department_id '0', described as all employees, and follows returned pagination. Retains user_id, name, en_name, nickname, email, mobile, department_ids and open_id.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GET https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/contact/v3/users; returned records enter the skill's in-memory employeeCache.
data_operations.condition: A directory helper needs an absent or stale cache. Freshness is checked after one hour on later access; TTL does not actively delete records. Lookup names are matched locally rather than sent as search parameters.

data_operations.operation: Derive identity matches and return directory information
data_operations.source: lib/employees.mjs resolution, display, listing and search helpers
data_operations.data_scope: Case-insensitive name/alias matches and whitespace-token-to-user_id associations; duplicate index keys overwrite previous mappings. Employee lookup/list/search can return complete cached records; search also examines email.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local lookup maps and the invoking caller. No additional remote recipient is specified for these returns.
data_operations.condition: When the corresponding helper is invoked. Async helpers can trigger directory retrieval; getDisplayNameSync only reads existing memory.

data_operations.operation: Start asynchronous name resolution but fail before CLI mutations
data_operations.data_scope: Supplied names enter resolveNames; its Promise is destructured without await, leaving resolved and unresolved undefined.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local execution; asynchronous lookup can initiate authentication or directory work, but completion is unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Named creation branches fail before main executes. Both membership-manager scripts fail before their add/remove calls, including their direct-ID combinations. Creation with only direct-ID options bypasses this defect.

data_operations.operation: Create a remote event and add attendees
data_operations.data_scope: Title, description, converted start/end timestamps, timezone, location and selected/default calendar. Sets private visibility and can_modify_event attendee ability. Adds supplied attendee IDs plus BOYANG_USER_ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Lark Calendar API and the selected remote calendar; attendee access and notifications are requested for the resulting membership.
data_operations.condition: Successful library invocation or creation CLI without the named-resolution failure. Boyang's inclusion is an explicit business rule. Event creation precedes a separate attendee request, with no rollback shown if that request fails.

data_operations.operation: Create a remote task with assignee memberships
data_operations.data_scope: Title, description, due timestamp in milliseconds and supplied assignee user_ids. Sets assignee roles and a 30-minute reminder; timezone is used locally for conversion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: POST https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/task/v2/tasks and the remotely created task.
data_operations.condition: Successful library invocation or creation CLI without the named-resolution failure. Reminder delivery and content are controlled externally.

data_operations.operation: Update selected event or task fields
data_operations.data_scope: Resource identifiers and supplied title/description; event location and start/end timestamps with timezone, or task due timestamp. Task update_fields enumerates the selected fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: PATCH requests to the applicable Lark Calendar or Task resource; returned resource stays with the caller.
data_operations.condition: On update invocation. Unspecified content fields are omitted; the functions still issue requests when no update fields are supplied.

data_operations.operation: Add or remove remote membership associations
data_operations.source: Calendar attendee and task-member library functions
data_operations.data_scope: Calendar/event or task identifiers and selected user_ids; task members have assignee roles. Calendar additions/removals set need_notification to true.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Lark Calendar attendees or attendees/batch_delete endpoints; Lark Task add_members or remove_members endpoints. Calendar attendee notifications are requested.
data_operations.condition: Direct library calls; createEvent also invokes attendee addition. Packaged manager CLIs fail before these calls. These functions do not enforce Boyang inclusion.

data_operations.operation: Request remote event or task deletion
data_operations.source: deleteEvent and deleteTask, including deletion CLIs
data_operations.data_scope: Selected calendar/event or task identifiers. Event deletion includes a notification preference.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: DELETE requests to Lark Calendar or Task resources; event-attendee notifications are requested by default.
data_operations.condition: Explicit deletion invocation. Event notifications can be disabled through the library argument or CLI --no-notify. A successful response is treated as deletion success; retention or irreversible erasure is not demonstrated.

data_operations.data_scope: Selected resource identifiers or listing parameters; API-returned event/task records. Calendar listing defaults to today through seven days later and page_size 50. Task listing defaults to 50 with an optional page token.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Applicable Lark GET endpoints; returned records remain with the invoking caller.
data_operations.condition: Explicit get/list invocation. Calendar listing and task listing each make one page request; employee retrieval separately follows all offered pages.

data_operations.operation: Send an empty update for attempted task completion
data_operations.data_scope: Task identifier, empty task object and empty update_fields array.
data_operations.condition: Only when completeTask is invoked directly. It supplies no completion field; whether an empty PATCH has any external effect is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Expose optional message-send and reply operations
data_operations.data_scope: Caller-provided message content and messageId, or receiveId and receiveIdType.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Lark IM message/reply endpoints, targeting the caller-selected message, chat or user.
data_operations.condition: Only explicit invocation of these exported helpers. No supplied script invokes them; calendar/task operations do not automatically send these messages.

data_operations.operation: Print command inputs and results to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Creation titles, times, timezone, attendee/assignee identifiers and event location; returned identifiers, titles, links and attendees. Event listings include location and up to 100 description characters. Selected JSON modes print complete returned objects.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling process stdout. No file persistence or additional remote recipient is specified.
data_operations.condition: On reachable command paths. Full creation JSON requires truthy JSON_OUTPUT; full listing JSON requires --json.

data_operations.operation: Serialize API failures into exceptions and diagnostics
data_operations.source: API wrapper, employee fallback handler and CLI catch handlers
data_operations.data_scope: Complete failed authentication/API response objects embedded in error messages. API failures also attach larkResponse, which CLI handlers print again. Employee diagnostics print failure messages, fallback status and cache counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local exception caller, stderr and status/count stdout; downstream log retention is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: On the corresponding failure or cache-load path. Exact response contents are unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: All accessible root-department directory pages for a request concerning one or a few employees.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Lark Contact API responses entering the skill process and employeeCache.
potential_excess.condition: Name resolution, individual employee lookup or display-name lookup with an absent/stale cache; excludes expressly requested whole-directory listings.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Automatic name-to-user_id resolution is declared; exhaustive root-directory retrieval is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the requested employees while preserving supported aliases and fallback behavior.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a suitably scoped lookup if the API supports it. Otherwise retain only relevant matches after scanning, and preserve the existing creation paths that accept direct IDs without directory resolution.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: A narrower remote query must support the required matching behavior and directory coverage. Its availability is not established by the supplied source; the retrieval itself may remain necessary.

potential_excess.data_scope: email, mobile, department_ids and open_id retained during ordinary name resolution.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: The in-memory employeeCache; complete records can subsequently be returned through directory helpers.
potential_excess.condition: Successful dynamic directory retrieval for name resolution. Email additionally supports the separate searchEmployees helper.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The name index uses name, en_name and nickname mapped to user_id. These additional fields are not needed for that outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain identifiers and supported name/alias fields for resolution.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project name-resolution records to those fields. Load email only for explicitly needed email search, and separate any expressly requested detailed-record access. Release unused cache references rather than treating TTL as deletion.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep additional fields only for callers that actually require detailed employee records or email matching; those requirements are not declared for ordinary event/task name resolution.

potential_excess.data_scope: Organizational roles linked to employee names, aliases and user_ids in the documentation.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Public SKILL.md distribution and its readers.
potential_excess.condition: Whenever the package documentation is distributed or read.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Name resolution requires name/alias-to-ID mappings; the Role column does not participate in resolution or CRUD.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Document supported employee identifiers and aliases, and preserve the explicit Boyang attendance rule.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the Role column while retaining the necessary mappings and business rule.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: The executable fallback directory and name index do not use organizational roles.

potential_excess.data_scope: Entire failed API response objects, including any returned fields beyond an actionable error code/message.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Exception messages and caller stderr; no persistent logging destination is established.
potential_excess.condition: Authentication/API failures. For API failures handled by the CLIs, the same response is serialized in error.message and again as larkResponse.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failure reporting supports CRUD; unrestricted response dumping and duplicate serialization are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return one actionable diagnostic identifying the failed operation and error.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Select safe code/message fields and make redacted detailed diagnostics optional. Remove the second serialization of the same payload.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain sufficient troubleshooting context. Duplicate output is a redundant action; unnecessary response fields are extra data within the required diagnostic. Actual sensitive response contents remain unknown.

Registry/funding URLs in metadata do not establish runtime transmissions.

Lark's effective contact coverage, granted scopes, calendar access controls, notification/reminder contents and downstream recipients are not supplied. A narrower contact-query capability cannot be established.

External callers of optional directory and IM helpers, and any storage or forwarding of caller outputs, are not shown.
